# Parity contraction, its exact convex dual, and a centroid-capacity obstruction

This note investigates a proof route using barycentric density selection,
separately from the boundary rate framework. It proves a compact extremal
construction and its dual value formula, and excludes a precise proposed
depth bridge. None of the assertions proves OC.

## 1. Self-coupling convex-order maximality is automatically trivial

Let mu be any compact probability measure and pi a coupling of k copies
of mu, with positive barycentric weights lambda_i of sum one. Jensen gives

    integral f(sum_i lambda_i x_i) dpi <= integral f dmu

for every convex f. The diagonal coupling realizes equality and has
barycentric law mu itself. Consequently a scheme that merely replaces
a self-coupling by a convex-order dominating coupling can always choose
the diagonal law. If mu is uniform mixed-integer volume, this law already
has density one relative to that volume. The new density-selection
theorem alone therefore supplies no contraction, preferred center, or
strict geometric improvement for an unrestricted self-coupling.

This observation does not refute an optimization with additional
constraints, but any such constraint must be specified and proved.

## 2. A quadratic-minimal contraction with at most one point per parity

Let S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d) be compact and nonempty, and let mu
be any probability measure supported on S. Let Q be any positive
definite quadratic form on the full ambient space. The set

    N={nu: nu is a probability on S and nu<=_cx mu}

is nonempty and compact. Indeed mu belongs to it, probabilities on the
compact S form a compact set, and every convex-order comparison is a
closed constraint. Thus integral Q dnu has a minimizer nu_* in N.

**Lemma.** The support of nu_* contains at most one physical point
above each integer parity class. In particular it contains at most 2^n
points. If P_* is the set of their integer bases, every point of P_*
is a vertex of conv(P_*), and

    conv(P_*) intersect Z^n=P_*.                    (1)

**Proof.** Suppose two different support points have same-parity bases.
Choose disjoint sufficiently small neighborhoods fixing their respective
base labels, separated by a positive distance. Their restrictions have
positive masses. Scale the larger restriction down to obtain submeasures
gamma_1,gamma_2 of equal mass m>0, with disjoint supports. Couple them,
for example by their normalized product, and let rho be the midpoint law.
Every midpoint belongs to C by convexity and has integer base by parity.
Thus

    nu'=nu_*-gamma_1-gamma_2+2rho

is a probability on S. Jensen gives nu'<=_cx nu_*<=_cx mu. The quadratic
identity

    Q(x)+Q(y)-2Q((x+y)/2)=Q(x-y)/2

shows a strictly positive decrease of its Q objective, contradicting
minimality. This also rules out two distinct points within one fiber.
There are only 2^n parity classes, so the support is finite.

Now suppose a nontrivial convex combination of distinct support bases
is an integer p. Use the same coefficients on their physical support
points to get a point y in S. Remove a sufficiently small common mass
times those coefficients from the corresponding positive atoms and put
all that mass at y. Jensen preserves convex-order feasibility, while
strict convexity of Q strictly lowers the objective. This contradiction
excludes both a support base lying in the convex hull of the others and
any other integer point of conv(P_*), proving (1). QED.

The finite base compression in (1) has an archived counterpart in
`candidate 7e12497595d939f1`, and the stronger actual
convex-piece realization is in
`candidate edf02845b3275e8c`. The present proof
retains full physical convex-order feasibility and an arbitrary specified
positive quadratic objective. It does not present the parity count as a
new replacement for those established partition results.

One atom has mass at least 2^(-n). Convex order permits a martingale from
nu_* to mu, so that atom is the barycenter of a submeasure of mu having
at least that mass. Such a submeasure is not thereby uniform or
log-concave. Applying the d-dimensional centroid Grünbaum inequality to
it would require an additional theorem.

## 3. Exact dual value; attainment is not silently presumed

Write V=min_(nu in N) integral Q dnu. Then

    V=sup_(phi finite convex)
         [min_(y in S)(Q(y)+phi(y))-integral phi dmu]. (2)

The supremum need not be treated as attained in this argument.

For the easy inequality, if nu<=_cx mu, then

    integral Q dnu
       >=min_S(Q+phi)-integral phi dnu
       >=min_S(Q+phi)-integral phi dmu.

For the reverse, fix t<V. There is no probability nu on S with
integral Q dnu<=t and all convex-order constraints. Compactness gives
a finite list phi_1,...,phi_r for which these finitely many inequalities
are already infeasible. Separate the compact convex set

    {(integral Q dnu,
       integral phi_1 dnu-integral phi_1 dmu,...,
       integral phi_r dnu-integral phi_r dmu): nu probability on S}

from the closed lower orthant (-infinity,t] times (-infinity,0]^r.
Strict separation has nonnegative coefficients a_0,...,a_r and gives

    inf_nu [a_0 integral Q dnu
                +sum_j a_j(integral phi_j dnu-integral phi_j dmu)]
        >a_0 t.

The coefficient a_0 is positive: if it were zero, the feasible test
nu=mu would make the left side at most zero. Divide by a_0 and use
phi=sum_j(a_j/a_0)phi_j. The infimum over probabilities on S is the
minimum of Q+phi on S, so the expression in (2) exceeds t. Let t
increase to V. This proves (2) without a minimax interchange or a dual
attainment claim.

Equivalently, the dual maximizes integral h dmu over finite concave
functions h satisfying h<=Q on S. Indeed h=alpha-phi with
alpha=min_S(Q+phi) has this property. Conversely any such h gives a
valid lower bound, and its associated phi=-h can only improve it by
the harmless additive contact normalization.

## 4. Exactly what an attained dual would say about target geometry

This section is an explicit conditional equality characterization,
not an assertion that the supremum in (2) is attained. Suppose a
finite concave dual function h attains V, and let nu_* be an optimal
primal law. Then

    integral Q dnu_* >= integral h dnu_*
                      >= integral h dmu=V

has equality throughout. Therefore every positive source atom y_i
satisfies Q(y_i)=h(y_i). For any martingale from nu_* to mu, its
conditional target probability P_i has mean y_i and

    integral h dP_i=h(y_i).                        (3)

Compact convex-order martingale existence is the previously proved
equal-mass case in
`candidate 6eda5637cc09a539`.
Alternatively the following description holds for any given such
martingale and needs no existence theorem of its own.

Choose a supporting affine majorant ell_i of the finite concave h at
y_i. The nonnegative function ell_i-h has P_i integral zero by (3),
so P_i is supported on the closed convex contact set

    E_i={x: h(x)=ell_i(x)}.                         (4)

This is actual convex geometry. It is weaker than claiming that P_i
is uniform volume on E_i. Distinct contact sets can overlap on whole
integer fibers, because an ambient tie hyperplane may carry positive
mixed measure; then their conditional target allocations need not be
indicator functions. Even a genuine uniform mixed measure on a convex
contact piece is still mixed, rather than an ordinary d-dimensional
uniform body.

The archived exact counterexample
`candidate d0cb383fd9782a9f`
already rules out the generic claim that all pieces of an exhaustive
2^n-piece integer-centroid convex partition can be made gamma_d-deep
at their own centroids. Its actual interval family has lengths 1,2,3
at bases 0,1,2. Every permissible two-piece partition has a mass-four
piece whose centroid admits an own-piece cap of mass 7/4<2. This is
not a counterexample specifically to all the extra dual conditions
above; it identifies the additional step that a dual-based approach
would actually need to prove, rather than assuming local Grünbaum
from convex cells alone.

## 5. Exact failure of the density-capped centroid bridge

The following tempting implication is FALSE:

    nu probability on S, nu<=2^n mu/mu(S),
    centroid(nu)=y in S
       => depth_S(y)>=2^(-n)gamma_d.               (5)

Here mu is the original uniform mixed measure. An exact example already
has n=d=1 and full-dimensional interval fibers. Let

    C={ (z,x): z>=0, x>=0, z+x<=10 },
    S=C intersect (Z times R),
    mu=H_1 restricted to S.

At integer z=0,...,10 the fiber is [0,10-z], so

    mu(S)=sum_(z=0)^10(10-z)=55.

Let nu be normalized mixed measure on the smaller triangular mixed
set T={z,x>=0,z+x<=7} intersect (Z times R). Its mass is 28. Thus

    nu=(1/28) mu restricted to T,
    dnu/d(mu/55)=55/28<2.                          (6)

For a triangular mixed set of integer size m, direct summation gives

    integral z dmu_m=m(m-1)(m+1)/6,
    integral x dmu_m=m(m+1)(2m+1)/12,
    mu_m=m(m+1)/2.

Consequently for m=7 the centroid is

    y=(2,5/2),                                    (7)

which belongs to S. The closed oblique halfspace

    H={z+x<=9/2}

contains y on its boundary. It captures the interval lengths
9/2,7/2,5/2,3/2,1/2 at bases 0,...,4 and zero positive length
elsewhere. Its exact original normalized mass is therefore

    mu(S intersect H)/55=(25/2)/55=5/22<1/4
                             =2^(-1)gamma_1.       (8)

All fibers and the full ambient convex body are explicit; all boundary
intersections have zero one-dimensional fiber measure. There is no
approximation or numerical claim. The counterexample concerns the
particular capacity-to-centroid implication (5), not OC.

Its meaning for the new selection theorem is precise: convex-order
replacement does not change the first moment. Thus using the replacement
only to establish a density ceiling and then taking its centroid cannot
be a sufficient bridge. The old law or its marginals must supply some
additional structural property that rules out (6)-(8).

## 6. The density-only first-moment information is exactly a trimmed region

For any compact probability mu and c>=1, the means of probabilities
nu<=c mu form the compact convex trimmed-centroid region

    Z_(1/c)(mu)
      ={c integral x dsigma: 0<=sigma<=mu, sigma(S)=1/c}. (9)

This is an equality simply by sigma=nu/c. Compactness follows from
weak compactness of dominated submeasures; convexity follows from
linearity of their moments. For a direction u its support function is

    sup_(y in Z_(1/c)) u.y
       =inf_(t in R) [t+c integral (u.x-t)_+ dmu].  (10)

To prove (10), any dominated sigma of mass 1/c satisfies
integral u.x dsigma<=t/c+integral(u.x-t)_+dmu. A threshold t for the
upper 1/c tail attains equality by selecting all mass above it and
the needed fraction at the threshold. Such a threshold exists for
any compact real-valued distribution, and splitting threshold mass
is allowed for dominated submeasures. This proves the exact support
formula, including atoms and closed boundary mass.

The stop-loss formula controls only first moments. Example (6)-(8)
shows that those exact moment constraints do not yield the desired
gamma_d/2^n cap inequality on a mixed convex set. The quadratic dual
route would have to use its contact equality (3)-(4), or another new
invariant, beyond this density-only information.

## 7. A valid shared-budget composition and an exact dual-contact obstruction

The audited ordinary theorem in
`candidate 660db01ed45063dd`
does combine with midpoint repair under the following explicit conditions.
Let K be an actual d-dimensional own fiber at integer base p, d>=1.
Suppose there are finitely many pairs of source submeasures
gamma_(j,-),gamma_(j,+), of equal pair masses m_j, whose total sum is
dominated by the original mixed measure AFTER removing the own volume
1_K dx. Thus all source credit is disjoint, including the own fiber.
Suppose each pair has a coupling whose physical midpoint law eta_j
lies on the fiber at p, and assume the literal SHARED measure budget

    eta=sum_j eta_j <=1_K dx.                      (11)

It is insufficient that each eta_j separately satisfy this inequality.
Define g as the centroid of 1_K dx+2eta. It belongs to K. The one-point
midpoint implication for every closed ambient halfspace H gives

    original_mass(H)>=|K intersect H_p|+eta(H_p).

The cited ordinary theorem applies to this very same eta and its actual
centroid. Consequently every closed H containing (p,g) satisfies

    original_mass(H)>(3/4)gamma_d (|K|+sum_j m_j).  (12)

Pure integer halfspaces containing the point contain all of K, and
the same conclusion follows from the full mass |K|+sum_j m_j in the
displayed cap-payment bound. The existing ordinary theorem supplies a
uniform positive surplus, so passage to the depth infimum is legitimate.
This is an actual shared-budget lemma; it assumes neither cap order
from convex order nor an OC statement on a contact piece.

The quadratic primal and dual contact conditions do NOT imply an
exhaustive representation of this kind. Take

    C=[-N,N] times K,       n=1, N>=2,

with K any positive d-dimensional convex body, centroid g_K, and
volume b. Normalize the mixed measure mu to probability. Its full
centroid y=(0,g_K) belongs to S. Jensen shows that delta_y is the
unique minimizer of integral |w|^2 dnu among nu<=_cx mu: every feasible
law has mean y and quadratic moment at least |y|^2, with equality only
for delta_y. The affine function

    h(w)=2y.w-|y|^2

satisfies h<=|w|^2 everywhere and attains the exact dual value. Its
contact region in the sense of (4) is the whole ambient space, so the
optimal martingale sends the one source y to the full original mu.
Thus both primal optimality and attained dual contact geometry are
present, with no attainment gap.

An exhaustive star of the type above would use own mass b and paired
endpoint mass 2 sum_j m_j=(2N)b. Hence sum_j m_j=Nb. But (11) forces
sum_j m_j<=b, impossible for N>=2. This is an exact shared-capacity
obstruction even for the uniquely minimal contracted law and its
attained affine dual. Separately valid midpoint repairs cannot be
summed as if they used independent copies of the own fiber's volume.

The product body satisfies OC, so the example excludes this particular
conversion from quadratic contact cells to an exhaustive dominated
centroid certificate. Additional source credit, multiple geometric
reference bodies, or a different cap inequality would be required.
